title: First Forty-Five Days Rapid Onramp Playbook
content:
Purpose: This playbook outlines a compact 45-day onboarding and adoption plan for mid-market customers moving from PoC to production with Redwood Inference. It’s intentionally prescriptive for CS + Solutions Eng to accelerate time-to-first-value (TTFV), surface renewal signals early, and create repeatable handoffs to growth/renewal.

Scope & When to use: Use for customers who have completed initial procurement and have a pilot or small production workload expected to ramp in 1–3 months. Not for enterprises requiring Private/on-prem compliance projects — those use the enterprise onboarding program.

High-level goals (45-day outcomes):
- Confirm production path (hosted | dedicated | private) and required SLAs.
- Deliver 1–2 measurable feature hits that prove ROI (e.g., search relevance improvement, internal automation saved hours, or chat latency targets met).
- Customer able to call Redwood API or Dedicated endpoint in daily workflows with successful authentication, basic observability, and warm cache patterns defined.
- Establish adoption metrics baseline and renewal-health scorecard.

Primary success metrics (sample tracking):
- Activation: First successful authenticated inference call and sample production traffic (>= 1k tokens/day or 200 embeddings/day depending on use case).
- Quality: Eval pass rate on critical prompt set >= 85% (customer-defined golden prompts).
- Reliability: 99% successful responses in a 7-day window (excluding planned maintenance).
- Engagement: 3 cross-functional users (PM/Eng/ops) routinely using the console or API within 30 days.
- Business impact: At least one quantified KPI improvement (time saved, conversion uplift) tracked in QBR.

Cadence & milestone summary (by day ranges):
- Day 0–3 (Kickoff & fastchecks)
  - Kickoff meeting: align objectives, roles, and success metrics. Invite: CS, SE, customer PM, customer Eng, ENG-SRE if infra changes expected.
  - Deliverable: project tracker with owners, access checklist (API keys, VPC peering info if needed), and immediate blockers list.
  - Quick checks: credentialing works, minimal example request returns, and a sanity test on chosen model variant.

- Day 4–14 (Technical enablement and quick wins)
  - SE runbook: integration recipes (Python SDK snippet, curl examples, best-practice headers for streaming). Attach sample prompt templates and cost estimates for early usage patterns.
  - Observability: instrument basic tracing and alert hooks in Console. Set token/spend alerts and latency SLO dashboards.
  - Quick win experiment: run a scoped eval comparing baseline outputs to Redwood model variant; prioritize one prompt set.
  - Outcome: first production-like request pattern verified and a short tech note in the project tracker.

- Day 15–30 (Adoption ramp & feature shipping)
  - Customer-facing adoption workshop: review prompt engineering best practices, batching strategies, and caching opportunities to lower unit cost.
  - Operationalize rollouts: define canary route, fallback model variant, and autoscale thresholds for Dedicated customers.
  - Run a short A/B on response templates or reranking to measure lift.
  - Outcome: measurable delta on chosen KPI (even if small), and runbook created for day-to-day ops.

- Day 31–45 (Scale, measurement, and QBR prep)
  - Scale checklist: verify autoscaling behavior, validate KV/prefix caching patterns, ensure billing tags and cost allocation enabled.
  - Renewal signal check: compare usage growth, quality metrics, and executive sponsor engagement to renewal-health thresholds.
  - Prepare 45-day readout (mini-QBR): two slides per owner (CS: adoption + business KPIs; SE: reliability + tech risks; Customer: success stories & open asks).
  - Outcome: 45-day readout delivered; next-step recommendation (expand usage, commit to Dedicated, or plan for renewal discussion).

Renewal-health signals & escalation rules (early warning system):
- Green: usage and quality trending up; sponsor actively engaged. No action required beyond normal cadence.
- Yellow (requires playbook): usage flat or <50% projected; quality regressions on golden prompts; only one stakeholder engaged. Action: 1-week focus burst with SE to unblock, run targeted prompt evals, share quick wins with stakeholders.
- Red (escalate to AM & CS lead): declining usage, repeated reliability incidents, or procurement/budget hold. Action: immediate exec sync, create mitigation plan, propose short-term price/commit incentive where appropriate.

Roles & responsibilities (concise):
- CS (owner): overall success plan, kickoff, stakeholder map, business KPI capture, 45-day readout.
- Solutions Eng (SE): integration support, prompt engineering sessions, evaluate and recommend model variants and batching/cache settings.
- Customer Eng/Ops: apply infra changes (VPC peering, firewall rules), validate autoscaling.
- SRE (if required): review observability hooks and SLA tests.

Checklists (quick inline):
- Before kickoff: NDA (if required), account creation, API key issuance, internal access list, primary business use-case summary.
- First week: sample request passing, SDK integrated, console access given, basic dashboard created.
- By day 30: golden prompt eval completed, A/B or rerank test results, initial cost estimate for monthly run-rate.
- By day 45: produce the 45-day readout, adoption baseline, renewal-health score, and next-step recommendation.

Meeting templates (short):
- Kickoff (30-45m): intros (5m) | objectives & success metrics (10m) | tech checklist & access items (10m) | immediate blockers & next steps (10m)
- Weekly sync (30m): metrics dashboard review (10m) | action items/blockers (10m) | focused technical topic (10m)
- 45-day readout (20-30m): one-page adoption summary + top 3 asks (SE/CS) + next steps and commitment options.

Sample email snippets (for CS to send after kickoff):
- Subject: Redwood Onramp — Next steps & access
  Hi <Customer-Name> team, great to kick off today. Attached is the tracker with owners and the SDK snippets we discussed. Please confirm the API key we created is working by responding with a successful sample request by EOD Thursday. — Sofia

- Subject: 45-day readout prep request
  Hi <Sponsor>, we’re preparing a short readout for day 45. Could you share the top business metric you want us to prioritize (e.g., time saved, conversion uplift)? Also confirm the attendees for the readout. Thanks.

Known risks and mitigation
- Risk: Customer engineering bandwidth is low.
  Mitigation: Propose managed integration hours from Solutions Eng for the first two sprints; push for product owner pairing session.
- Risk: Cost surprises from heavy inference usage.
  Mitigation: Enable spend alerts, recommend batching and caching patterns, provide a 2-week cost simulation.
- Risk: Quality regression after model upgrade.
  Mitigation: Create a canary route and rollout policy; tie eval regression alerts to a slack channel for immediate response.

Notes to self / TODOs
- Add standard cost-simulation sheet link here (confluence id: CONFL-COST-SIM-21).
- Build one-click invite template to reduce kickoff lead time.
- Follow up with product-hosted-api on recommended default model variants for classification workloads.

Appendix: Quick adoption checklist (copyable)
- [ ] Kickoff scheduled
- [ ] API key issued & verified
- [ ] SDK example run
- [ ] Console access & dashboard created
- [ ] Golden prompt set defined
- [ ] Eval run complete
- [ ] Autoscale and canary configured (for Dedicated)
- [ ] 45-day readout scheduled

References and links
- Internal: Confluence onboarding baseline: CONFL-7421
- Template: onboarding project tracker template (github repo link in linked_artifacts)
- Slack: #cs-onboarding channel

This document is a working draft intended for CS + SE collaboration; please comment inline with improvements and any additional checks we should add for edge cases (VPC peering delays, HSM/KMS key rotation, data-retention compliance asks).
